sheet-1.description: The lower two thirds of the sheet is the centre of Ashland, a small railroad village in Voorhees Township, Camden County, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It covers Magnolia Avenue or Evesham Road, the township line between Delaware Township to the north and Voorhees Township to the south, from Ashland and Alpha Avenues in the west to the open fields east of Haddonfield Avenue. North of the road it reaches Ellis Avenue, Railroad Boulevard and the large lots numbered 40, 43 and 44; south of it, Mansion, Haddonfield and Atlantic Avenues run down to Fairview and Lotus Avenues. The West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) crosses the map from north to south as a band of four tracks, with Ashland Station and a freight house beside it on the south side of the road. Just west of the line is the Charles F. Ober coal yard with a steel and frame trestle, scale and office, and an auto repairing shop. The fire department stands on Alpha Avenue at the western edge. On Evesham Road near Railroad Boulevard are a concrete block garage, stores and the post office. The rest of the area is frame dwellings on deep lots, with sheds and hen houses; much of the eastern half is unbuilt. The upper third of the sheet, outside this part, carries a key map of the whole village at about 800 feet to an inch, a state locator map, the legend, the index of specials and the title cartouche dated April 1925.
notes: Magnolia Avenue or Evesham Road is today West Evesham Road and East Evesham Road (County Route 544).
Haddonfield Avenue is today Burnt Mill Road.
Ashland Avenue north of Evesham Road is today Ogden Avenue at this point; Alpha Avenue keeps its name.
Atlantic Avenue beside the railroad is not in OpenStreetMap today.
Delaware Township, north of Evesham Road, was renamed Cherry Hill Township in 1961.
The West Jersey and Seashore Railroad is today the NJ Transit Atlantic City Line, with the PATCO line alongside.
Mansion Avenue jogs at Fairview Avenue; the junction was not used as control.

map. Scale 100 ft. Top third is a key map of the whole village (about 800 ft to an inch), the index of specials and the title cartouche: not configured, masked out. One part: the 100 ft map below the heavy line, Magnolia Av or Evesham Rd from Ashland/Alpha Av east past Haddonfield Av (now Burnt Mill Road), Ellis Av, Railroad Blvd, Mansion Av, Fairview Av, Lotus Av; W.J.&S.R.R. (now Atlantic City Line and PATCO) crosses it.

sheet-2.description: The western part of Ashland, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The map runs from Magnolia Avenue or Evesham Road, along the top, south to Prospect Avenue and a diagonal property line at the foot, and from the Branch of Coopers Creek in the west to Alpha Avenue in the east. The road is also the township line, with Delaware Township to the north and Voorhees Township to the south; west of the creek, crossed by a concrete bridge, the line continues between Centre and Clementon Townships, and the creek itself divides Centre and Clementon Townships. The streets form a regular grid: Fairview, Lotus and Homer Avenues run east to west, crossed by West End, Ebert, Preston and Alpha Avenues, with Perot and Ashland Avenues leaving northwards from the road at the top right. A stretch of Homer Avenue west of West End Avenue is marked not open. The blocks are laid out in narrow house lots, but building is sparse: scattered frame dwellings, most of one or two storeys, with sheds, hen houses and a wagon shed, and a few brick-veneered houses on Homer Avenue. Large blocks in the south and west, numbered 51, 56, 63, 64, 66 and 70, are almost empty. There are no industrial or public buildings on this part. The adjoining sheets are marked 1 on the east and 3 on the north.
notes: Magnolia Avenue or Evesham Road is today West Evesham Road (County Route 544).
Ashland Avenue north of Evesham Road is today Ogden Avenue at this point.
Delaware Township was renamed Cherry Hill Township in 1961; Centre Township is now divided among several boroughs.
Homer Avenue west of West End Avenue is marked not open.

map. Scale 100 ft. One part: west side, Magnolia Av or Evesham Rd south to the Prospect Av line, West End, Ebert, Preston, Alpha Avs; Branch of Coopers Creek on the west with the Centre/Clementon township line.

sheet-3.description: The northern part of Ashland, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, on both sides of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad), which crosses the sheet from north to south a little east of centre. West of the line is a planned subdivision of curving streets: Morrill Terrace, Eleanor Terrace and Ward Terrace form a loop crossed by Dobson Lane, Henzey Lane and Orchard Lane, with Ashland Avenue running along the railroad and Perot Avenue leaving southwards at the bottom left. Its lots are laid out but mostly empty, with a few dwellings. Between Ward Terrace and the railroad, in block 40, stands the works of Cramm and Priceturner, manufacturers of concrete tile, with dry rooms and a water tank. East of the line, between Railroad Boulevard and Haddonfield Avenue, are the numbered avenues 1st to 7th, set at a slant towards the north, with Henzey, Hoffman, Kassner and Ellis Avenues to the south. These blocks are divided into narrow lots and carry frame dwellings, barns and hen houses; blocks 35, 37 and 41 are large and almost empty. The western and eastern margins (blocks 19, 26, 38, 25 and 33) are left blank apart from their numbers and a few buildings near Haddonfield Avenue. The sheet adjoins sheet 2 at the bottom left and sheet 1 at the bottom.
notes: Haddonfield Avenue is today Burnt Mill Road.
Henzey Lane is spelled Henszey Lane in OpenStreetMap; Henzey Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap today.
3rd Avenue is South 3rd Avenue and 6th Avenue West 6th Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Ashland Avenue south of Ward Terrace is today Ogden Avenue.
Railroad Boulevard is drawn 25 ft wide; its modern right-of-way centre lies 3 to 7 m west of the drawn street, so it was not used as control here.
The West Jersey and Seashore Railroad is today the NJ Transit Atlantic City Line, with the PATCO line alongside.
